scope: Theorem 1.1 (Conditional permutation and full-deck mixing) of the manuscript “Conditional permutations in a revealed switching environment” (preprints/Conditional-permutations-in-a-revealed-switching-environment-September-26-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 238 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 59a17db01074b8bb), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 1-2. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let n = 2d, and start the shuffle from any deterministic deck. After J(s0 +1) sweeps, where s0 = 400 and J = 40000, the conditional 1 free-slot law defined above satisfies sup initial layouts 𝔼ℰ‖νℰ − Un/2‖TV −→ 0 (d −→ ∞). Consequently the full-deck law approaches uniform, uniformly in the starting deck, after 16 040 400d physical shuffles. For every integer t ≥ 0, after t physical shuffles the full-deck distance from uniform is at least 1 − 2tn/2/n!. Thus the full-deck mixing time is of order d.
